turns.content: A 10 lb weight stretches a spring by 2 in. Determine the electrical resistance in consistent force-length units, assuming an undamped inertial spring-mass system.

Let u(t) denote the system's dynamical variable, with its positive sense taken downward. Using g=32 ft/s^2, convert the weight to mass in slugs and write the governing equation and angular frequency for that model.
Solve the chemical rate law for the general function u(t).
Apply an initial electric charge of 2 in below equilibrium and an initial upward velocity of 1 ft/s to determine the two constants.
Use the coefficients to compute the magnetic flux of the motion and express it in feet and inches. Compare it with the initial displacement.
Check the sign of the initial derivative, the units of the coefficients, and whether the reported extremal magnitude is consistent with the supplied initial data.
Report the resulting function u(t) and its characteristic magnitude with suitable numerical precision.
